tasks.short: Explain the test to the patient, answer questions about preparation by phone before the test, and note in the record that the patient was informed.

steps.what: Cardiovascular technologist explains testing procedures to patients to reduce anxiety
Cardiovascular technologist answers patients' questions about test preparation by phone
Cardiovascular technologist notes in the record that the patient was informed

tasks.design: Each test has an information page with a short video in the patient portal ({OTHER}), linked from the appointment, covering preparation and what will happen, so fewer patients phone with preparation questions. The technologist records that the patient was informed as today. Explaining the test at the start stays with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation questions came by phone and information was noted in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient portals host information pages and videos per test.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who do not use the portal still call.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a frightened patient before a stress test.

evidence.claim: Patient portals can host information pages and videos linked to appointments.
Providers must inform patients about care and record it in the dossier.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient arrived to information recorded; the test is outside.
Input contract: information page per test; fallback is phone questions.
Patients read or watch the page before the test; a little patient time is priced.

Explaining at the start and recording that the patient was informed keep their full time; a tick box instead of a note is not a saving. s2 keeps 60 because fewer patients phone with preparation questions.
research_questions: Do tests cancelled for poor preparation fall?

incremental.description: Cardiovascular technologist keeps the information pages current.
Patients read the information page before the test.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients open the page, so most still phone (s2 keeps 85) (1.0); high: many first-time patients use the page (3.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attach leads and set up monitoring, watch blood pressure and heart rate on the EKG during the procedure, notify the physician of abnormal readings, and write readings in the procedure log.

steps.what: Cardiovascular technologist attaches leads and sets up EKG monitoring
Cardiovascular technologist monitors patients' blood pressure and heart rate during procedures
Cardiovascular technologist notifies the physician if something appears wrong
Cardiovascular technologist writes readings in the procedure log

tasks.design: The patient monitor sends readings at set intervals and on events to the procedure record ({OTHER}), so the technologist does not write them in a log; the technologist adds a note only for events. Setting up, watching the patient and notifying the physician stay with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were copied from the monitor into a log by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient monitors export readings to the record.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a patient go pale before the numbers change.

evidence.claim: Patient monitors can export readings to the record at intervals and on events.
Medical-purpose software is a medical device; a plain data link here does not interpret readings.

assumptions: Boundary: from the procedure start to readings logged; the physician's decisions are outside.
Input contract: monitor linked to the record; fallback is the paper log.

incremental.description: Cardiovascular technologist checks the export started at each procedure.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older monitors in half of the rooms are not linked, so readings are still written there (s4 keeps 60) (5.5); high: linked monitors in every room (11.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check the patient's identity, ask about medical history and medication, type the answers into the test system, and enter test results into the record.

steps.what: Patient fills the history and medication questionnaire in the patient portal before the visit
Cardiovascular technologist obtains patient identification at the desk
Cardiovascular technologist asks about medical history and medication: from scratch today; confirming and adding to the patient's questionnaire answers after the change
Cardiovascular technologist types the history answers into the test system
Cardiovascular technologist records test results: typed into the record today; sent by the device and completed by hand where needed after the change
Cardiovascular technologist checks the device results attached to the record: patient, test type and values against the device
Cardiovascular technologist releases the checked results to the patient record

tasks.design: Patients fill a history and medication questionnaire in the patient portal before the visit, and the answers and the record's medication list appear in the test system ({OTHER}), so the technologist confirms and adds to them instead of asking from scratch and typing. Test results go from the EKG, echo or stress-test device to the record through an integration instead of being typed; the technologist checks patient, test and values and releases them once. Checking identity stays with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: History was asked from scratch and typed, and results retyped from the device.
tasks.enabler_now: Portals take pre-visit questionnaires; test devices export results to the record.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the symptom the patient left off the form.
tasks.altitude: The technologist confirms data instead of typing it.

evidence.claim: Test devices can export results to the record, and portals can take pre-visit questionnaires.
Health data are special category data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient arrived to results recorded; reporting the test is outside.
Input contract: devices linked to the record; fallback is typing.

Patients fill the questionnaire before the visit (s0); their time is shown there and is outside the technologist's savings. s2 keeps 60 because the technologist confirms and adds to the answers with the patient; the results check and release keep their full time.
research_questions: Do transcription errors in results fall?

incremental.description: No new work: confirming answers with the patient is in s2's remaining time, and the patient's time is in s0.

approvals.approved_version: The test results with patient, test type and values exactly as checked by the technologist in s4c, released once to this patient's record; any correction needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older devices are not linked (s4 keeps 60) and few patients fill the questionnaire (s2 keeps 85, s3 keeps 70) (22.5); high: linked devices and most questionnaires filled (50.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch the patient's comfort and responses during the test, alert the physician to abnormalities, and record incidents and responses in the test report.

steps.what: Cardiovascular technologist monitors patients' comfort and safety during tests
Cardiovascular technologist alerts physicians to abnormalities or changes in patient responses
Cardiovascular technologist records incidents and patient responses in the test report as free text

tasks.design: The test report ({OTHER}) gets pick lists for common patient responses (chest pain, dizziness, test stopped early and why) with time stamps from the device, and the technologist records each response and incident as today. Watching the patient and alerting the physician stay with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Responses and incidents were written in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Test reports can hold pick lists with device time stamps.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual events still need free text.
tasks.human_edge: Stopping a test because a patient's face says something is wrong.

reach.learn: Whether patient responses are recorded consistently.

evidence.claim: Test reports can hold pick lists for patient responses with time stamps.

assumptions: Boundary: from the test running to responses recorded; treatment of events is outside.
Input contract: pick lists set up; fallback is free text.
Watching patients and alerting the physician keep their full time. s3 keeps 85 because only the device time stamps fill in; picking a response instead of typing it is not a saving.

incremental.description: No new work: writing free text for unusual events is in s3's remaining time.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: device time stamps are often missing, so times are still typed (s3 keeps 95) (0.7); high: busy stress-test lists with device times (2.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The cardiovascular technologist keeps explaining tests, watching patients and alerting physicians; phone questions, copied readings and typed history and results shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technologist with more time with patients.
